expert_diagnosis: Coffee Day Enterprises faced a compounding crisis of severe debt, a sudden catastrophic key-person loss, and creditor confidence collapse. The company's recovery required a complete leadership transition, creditor stabilization, and systematic non-core asset monetization while preserving the core café brand. Root causes: debt solvency pressure, key-person and founder dependency, governance and reputational crisis, creditor confidence risk, complex group and non-core asset burden, need for asset monetization, retail operating rationalization, and leadership transition risk.
expert_first_action: Immediate creditor communication and standstill to prevent panic defaults; install credible interim leadership and governance; preserve core café operations; identify and initiate sale of non-core assets; ring-fence café brand; develop transparent debt-reduction roadmap for lenders.
actual_decision: Successor leadership (Malavika Hegde) took over. The company pursued debt reduction through asset monetization, cost control, and business focus.
harmful_actions: Over-leveraged group structure created systemic vulnerability to single key-person loss
Excessive debt relative to core café business cash flows
beneficial_actions: Malavika Hegde installed as successor CEO providing credible governance continuity
Debt reduced from approximately ₹70 billion in 2019 to ₹4.65 billion by 2023
Core café brand preserved and operations continued
Cost control and business focus implemented
citation: Emerald 2025 case abstract: debt reduced from ~INR 70 billion in 2019 to INR 4.65 billion in 2023. Coffee Day Annual Report 2021 reported net debt ₹1,731 crore. Improvement attributed to debt reduction, asset monetization, cost control, business focus, operational restructuring.
actual_outcome: Successful debt turnaround. Debt reduced from approximately ₹70 billion in 2019 to ₹4.65 billion by 2023. Company continued operating. Malavika Hegde credited with leading the turnaround through asset monetization, cost control, and operational focus.
documented_root_causes: Debt solvency pressure — ₹70 billion in group debt
Key-person and founder dependency — founder death created governance vacuum
Governance and reputational crisis — sudden founder loss shook creditor confidence
Creditor confidence risk — founder was the credible counterparty
Complex group and non-core asset burden — required monetization
Need for asset monetization — only path to debt reduction
Retail operating rationalization — store footprint needed review
Leadership transition risk — successor had to be credible and decisive
final_business_state: Successful turnaround. Debt reduced ~94% by 2023. Company operating. Core brand preserved.
